voyage.name: Parc Maisonneuve and Jardin Botanique de Montreal
voyage.content: The Jardin Botanique is one of the largest botanical gardens in the world and features the First Nations Garden, the Insectarium, the Tree House, and 16 different themed gardens and greenhouses.

voyage.name: Parc du Mont-Royal
voyage.content: North of avenue des Pins, between avenue du Parc and chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges. This beautiful, immense urban park tops the "mountain" (at 232 m, it's more like a hill) that overlooks all of Montreal and lends the city its name. Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, creator of Central Park and Prospect Park in New York, the park is elegant and accessible, and has hundreds of nooks and crannies to explore. A broad and

voyage.name: Parc de l'Ile-de-la-Visitation
voyage.content: Rue d'Iberville and boulevard Gouin, (metro Henri-Bourassa, Bus 69 east). This regional park is along the Rivière-des-Prairies. Quiet and enjoyable place to bring a lunch and relax for an afternoon. Good starting point for a cycling tour along the river.

voyage.name: Just For Laughs Festival
voyage.content: Comedy festival with three main components: indoor paid shows (usually stand-up, but not always), free street theatre/comedy, and a mini film festival called Comedia. July.

voyage.name: Shakespeare-in-the-Park
voyage.content: During the summer in parks around Montreal, Repercussion Theatre puts on outdoor performances of Shakespeare plays free of charge.

voyage.name: Festival du Monde Arabe
voyage.content: In November, an annual festival celebrating the music and culture of the Arab world takes place in Montreal. Many Arab performers, traditional and modern, take the stage.

voyage.name: Festival Mondiale de la bière
voyage.content: Annually, in June: several days of tasting beers, ciders, and other beverages from all over Quebec, Canada and further afield. The event typically offers over 500 different beverages, from over 70 brewers, from many countries. There is no admission fee, and samples typically sell for 2-8 tickets ($1 a ticket) for a 150-200 ml sample. There are also musical performances and food kiosks. The festival can get very busy

voyage.name: Montréal en lumière
voyage.content: A relatively new wintertime affair, attempting to transplant the city's festival magic to the cold season. Includes three main categories of activities: food and wine, performing arts, and free activities both indoor and outdoor. February.

voyage.name: Montreal International Fireworks Competition
voyage.content: In La Ronde amusement park (in Parc Jean-Drapeau). This fantastic festival features full-length fireworks displays, accompanied by orchestral music, by national teams from about a dozen countries around the world. Although the hot seats are inside the La Ronde theme park, the fireworks are visible from pretty much any clear space or rooftop in the centre of the city. Pedestrians can watch from Jacques Cartier Bridge,

voyage.name: Fete de St-Jean-Baptiste
voyage.content: June 24 is Quebec's national holiday (Fête nationale). During the evening, a huge show takes place at Maisonneuve park. This is the show to go to hear made-in-Quebec music. Free. Street parties can also be found all over the city.

voyage.name: International Festival of Film on Art
voyage.content: Devoted to the promotion and presentation of the finest productions on art and media art. A ten-day competitive festival, it is the most important annual event of its kind in the world. FIFA has become a focal point for artists and artisans from the art and film communities, and for art and cinema enthusiasts.

voyage.name: Montreal International Jazz Festival
voyage.alt: Festival International de Jazz de Montréal
voyage.content: The world's largest jazz festival, this festival is a major international event, attracting many big name artists. Many streets in downtown Montreal are closed off to traffic for two weeks and several concert stages are set up. There are many free outdoor shows and indoor concerts (paid). Late June - early July.

voyage.name: POP Montréal International Music Festival
voyage.content: A massive feast of up-and-coming bands in a variety of popular genres. In early fall, host to more than 80 events, more than 300 artists, a conference, and an arts fair. POP Montreal showcases emerging and innovative artists alongside rising international stars and is committed to encouraging vibrant indie communities.

voyage.name: Francofolies
voyage.content: A festival celebrating French-language music from around the world. Similarly to the jazz festival, many free outdoor concerts are offered in a section of downtown that is closed off to traffic for a week. Mid-June.

voyage.name: MUTEK
voyage.content: An annual gathering, held in Montreal. The MUTEK festival showcases emerging forms of electronic music and the latest trends in sound creation.

voyage.name: Heavy Montréal
voyage.content: A two-day heavy music festival taking place in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène.

voyage.name: Osheaga Music and Arts Festival
voyage.content: A three-day indie & alternative rock festival held annually in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène at the end of July/beginning of August.

voyage.name: Fantasia
voyage.content: July.

voyage.name: Image + Nation
voyage.content: November/December.

voyage.name: Festival du nouveau cinéma de Montréal
voyage.alt: new filmmakers, well-known auteurs, new media
voyage.content: October.

voyage.name: Cinémania
voyage.content: November.

voyage.name: Les Rencontres internationales du documentaire de Montréal
voyage.content: November.

voyage.name: Les Rendez-vous du cinéma québécois
voyage.content: February.

voyage.name: Village des Valeurs
voyage.content: Second hand store providing montrealers with shops inside and outside of Montreal.

voyage.name: MEC
voyage.content: Mountain Equipment Co-op is a co-operative with staff who know the stores merchandise well.

voyage.name: La cordée
voyage.content: Great store to stock up on your favorite or some essential gear for your next outdoor activity.

voyage.name: Kanuk
voyage.content: Kanuk are best known for their winter coats and parkas.

voyage.name: Brasserie La Cage
voyage.content: Sports bar and grill. Great place to watch Montreal Canadiens hockey games, the atmosphere gets crazy during the NHL playoffs!

voyage.name: Les Trois Brasseurs
voyage.content: Microbrewery with a pub-style menu and a European flair.

voyage.name: Juliette et chocolat
voyage.content: Specialised in chocolate desserts and famed for its very rich drinking chocolate.

voyage.name: Rockaberry
voyage.content: Enormous portions of cakes, pies, crumbles and brownies.

voyage.name: Copper Branch
voyage.content: Vegan chain serving sandwiches, wraps, soups and some desserts.

voyage.name: Vieux-Port
voyage.address: South of rue Saint-Antoine between rue McGill and rue Berri
voyage.content: The Old Port is a large waterfront green space with attractions such as Cirque du Soleil, the Montreal Science Center, the Labyrinth, the Clock Tower, and a large outdoor audio-visual stage which is the site for the Canada Day fireworks.

voyage.name: Place Jacques-Cartier
voyage.content: Pedestrian street filled with street artists and musicians, and there are numerous fine restaurants and private art galleries nearby.

voyage.name: Notre-Dame Basilica
voyage.price: Adults $14, student (17-22) children (6-16) $9, children under 6 free
voyage.content: Probably the city's most spectacular church, a gem of Victorian Gothic. Service is at 17:00 daily and on Sunday morning. Entrance is free for worship, but donations are suggested. During service, the organ music is not to be missed. While it shouldn't have to be mentioned, tourists should be respectful during services. Photography is not allowed during services. 20-minute guided tours offered in French or English.

voyage.name: Montreal Clock Tower
voyage.hours: Early May and September (after Labour Day): Sat Sun 10:00-19:00; mid May-mid June and mid August-Labour Day: Mon-Thu 10:00-19:00, Fri-Sun 10:00-21:00; mid June-mid August: 10:00-21:00 daily
voyage.content: Also known as the Sailors' Memorial Clock, the clock tower was built between 1919-1922 as a memorial to sailors lost at sea. Its clock mechanism is similar to Big Ben's and was known for its accuracy; sailors would often set their watches by it. The clock tower is no longer open to visitors.

voyage.name: Former Parliament in Montreal
voyage.content: While Montreal was the capital of Canada from 1843 to 1849, it also hosted the parliament building. The building was burnt to the ground by rioters in 1849. Some of the artifacts uncovered from the site are displayed in a self-guided tour.

voyage.name: Marguerite-Bourgeoys Museum and Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Secours Chapel
voyage.content: Built in 1655, Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Secours, is the oldest stone church in Montreal. The museum houses artifacts from the church's history and pays tribute to Marguerite Bourgeoys, Montreal's first teacher.

voyage.name: Pointe-à-Callière Museum
voyage.alt: Montréal Museum of Archeology and History
voyage.hours: Labour Day to 24 June: Tue-Fri 10AM-5PM, Sat-Sun 11AM-5PM; 25 June to Labour Day: Mon-Fri 10AM-6PM, Sat-Sun 11AM-6PM
voyage.content: A modern museum built over the ruins of Montreal's first settlement, Pointe à Callière. This museum uses audiovisual technology as well as surrounding archaeological remains to tell the story of Montreal from the first natives to the present day.

voyage.name: Sir George-Étienne Cartier National Historic Site
voyage.price: $4.25/adult, $3.75/senior, youth free, $3.75 per person in commercial group
voyage.hours: June 17-Sep-4: Wed-Sun 10AM-5PM; Sept 5-Oct 31: Sat-Mon 10AM-5PM; Dec 1-17: Sat-Sun 10AM-5PM
voyage.content: Reconstruction of two 19th-century Victorian homes commemorating the life and accomplishments of Sir George-Étienne Cartier, who was a Canadian statesman and Father of Confederation.

voyage.name: Montréal Science Centre
voyage.price: IMAX screenings $8.50 child, $10.50 teen, $11.50 adult, $10.50 senior; exhibitions $8.50 child, $13 teen, $15 adult, $13 senior, $40 family; see website for details
voyage.hours: Daily 10:00-17:00; check listings for IMAX movie times
voyage.content: Interactive science museum and IMAX theater.

voyage.name: Centre d'histoire de Montréal
voyage.price: $6 adults, $5 seniors, $4 children (6-17) and students, $15 families, free for children under 6
voyage.content: Covering the history of Montreal from its founding in 1535. The museum is housed in a former fire station that dates from 1903.

voyage.name: Bank of Montréal Museum
voyage.content: Hands-on museum focusing on the history of banking in Montreal.

voyage.name: Château Ramezay Museum
voyage.content: 18th century Governor's residence and gardens full of historical artifacts from daily life.

voyage.name: DHC/ART
voyage.content: A privately endowed foundation, DHC/ART is a permanent location for exciting and relevant temporary visual arts exhibitions and projects.

voyage.name: Winter Ice Skating
voyage.price: $4 adults, $3 child (does not include skate rental)

voyage.name: Voiles en voiles
voyage.content: This venue offers a diverse range of outdoor activities, including aerial adventure courses, wall climbing, and inflatable games, all set within a thematic environment inspired by 18th-century pirate and royal ships.

voyage.name: Boutique des métiers d'art du Québec
voyage.content: Arts, crafts, and jewellery from over 100 Quebec artists.

voyage.name: Studio/Boutique gogo•glass
voyage.content: Hand blown glass by local artists Annie Michaud and Karine Bouchard. Demonstrations of glass blowing techniques.

voyage.name: Galerie de Chariot
voyage.content: Government-certified Inuit soapstone carvings and historical drawings.

voyage.name: L'Original
voyage.content: Non-profit gallery showing original works by several hundred living artists, many of them Montreal painters and street artists. Works are signed originals, not reproductions. A second location is on rue Saint-Denis in the Plateau.

voyage.name: Olive & Gourmando
voyage.content: Popular boulangerie offering fresh sandwiches, soups, and a daily lunch dish and baked goods. Also sells breads, jams, and snacks to take away.

voyage.name: Marché du Vieux
voyage.content: Equal parts bistro and fine-food boutique, Marché du Vieux is a cute spot for a gourmet lunch or snack.

voyage.name: Le Jardin Nelson
voyage.content: Fancy and filling crepes are the main draw to this historic restaurant and garden courtyard. Offering outdoor jazz and other live music in the summer, it loses some of its charm in the winter when things move inside.

voyage.name: Boris Bistro
voyage.hours: Summer: Mon-Fri 11:30-23:00, Sat Sun 12:00-23:00; winter: Lunch: Mon-Fri 11:30-14:00; dinner: Tue-Fri 17:00-23:00, Sat 18:00-23:00
voyage.content: Popular bistro featuring a large courtyard. Menu offers meats, seafood, and pastas. Try the French fries cooked in duck fat.

voyage.name: Restaurant Le Fripon
voyage.content: Grand historic building with shaded terrace serving French bistro fare, seafood, and pastas. Note the terrace menu is limited to soups, snails, and fries. Bar features wide selection of domestic and imported beers.

voyage.name: Chez Suzette
voyage.content: Crepes and fondue in a cozy, family-friendly spot. Wine and cider at SAQ prices + $5.

voyage.name: Sushi-ya
voyage.content: Well-executed and beautifully presented sushi and tempura in an elegant dining room. Staff speaks English as well as French.

voyage.name: Gibby's
voyage.content: Fancy steakhouse housed in a 200-year-old former stable, popular with tourists. Reservations strongly recommended.

voyage.name: Le Saint-Gabriel
voyage.content: French fine cuisine with a taste of Quebec from the first North America alcohol licence, issued in 1754.

voyage.name: Kyo Bar Japonais
voyage.hours: Lunch: Mon-Fri 11:30A-14:30; dinner: Mon-Thu 17:00-23:00, Fri Sat 17:00-00:00
voyage.content: Upscale Japanese restaurant and sushi bar with a menu based on izakaya classics and an extensive sake selection.

voyage.name: Toqué!
voyage.content: In 1993, chef Normand Laprise put Montreal cuisine on the map with this landmark restaurant, and after more than 25 years, it's still going strong in a new location. Combining the latest trends in fine dining with local and regional produce, the chefs create spectacularly complex dishes in tiny, but strangely satisfying portions. The house specialty is an eight-course surprise menu, made up of many small dishes. This

voyage.name: Pub St-Paul
voyage.content: Big space, popular with tours. Offers pub grub and a view of the river during the day and live music (Th-Sa 22:00). Cheap (for Old Montreal) and casual.

voyage.name: Santos
voyage.content: Cafe-by-day and bar-by-night, Santos is the place to escape your hotel lobby for a martini and late night snack of "Pop Food", their take on tapas. Live jazz on Thursdays, DJ on the weekends. Reservations recommended for Saturday nights. Weekend covers start around $20.

voyage.name: Wunderbar
voyage.content: Trendy spot on the edge of Old Montreal. Expect cover charges and a line at the door. Changing out of your sight-seeing clothes and into something swanky will probably help get you in the door.

voyage.name: Suite 701
voyage.content: "Suite" sums it up for this high-end lounge popular with the executive set. Leather couches and sipping scotches.

voyage.name: Alternative Hostel of Old Montreal
voyage.content: Housed in a 19th-century warehouse, this hostel boasts fair trade coffee, wi-fi, an organic continental breakfast, and a range of activities and classes. Kitchen and laundry facilities provided. Often full, reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Auberge Vieux Port
voyage.content: A good deal for the price, this historical building, set back from the street, books up early.

voyage.name: Le Westin Montreal
voyage.content: 454 large and well-appointed guestrooms at the gateway to Old Montreal. Each room features the ten-layer Heavenly Bed, and the hotel also offers a unique glass-bottom pool.

voyage.name: Hotel Epik Montreal
voyage.content: Three-star boutique hotel.

voyage.name: Trylon Hotels
voyage.content: A modern, renovated hotel. Rooftop terrace, lounge, indoor pool. 2 min from the entertainment district & grocery store.

voyage.name: Hotel St-Paul
voyage.content: This self-described "design hotel" in Old Montreal features uber-modern rooms on the edge of the historical district. See Eat and Drink for bars and restaurants in the same building.

voyage.name: Hotel Nelligan
voyage.content: Falling somewhere between posh and opulent, the Nelligan offers large rooms with king beds, loft-style suites, and rooftop two-room penthouses above a fine French restaurant. Some rooms with fireplaces, and jacuzzi-tubs for two.

voyage.name: Hotel Gault
voyage.content: Feels like you're stepping into Architectural Digest with ultra-modern furniture and rooms in a converted warehouse. Very helpful staff.

voyage.name: Le Saint Sulpice
voyage.content: Four-star boutique hotel offering four types of luxury suites.

voyage.name: Le Petit Hotel
voyage.content: A boutique hotel, Le Petit Hotel is charming, chic and hip in the middle of Old Montreal. It combines 19th-century architecture with 21st century tech such as Wi-Fi, iPod docking station, LCDs, Nintendo Wii and multi-jet showers.

voyage.name: W Montreal
voyage.content: A luxury hotel, the W Montreal has 152 rooms, spa, and a restaurant - Otto Ristorante. This hotel is between downtown and Old Montreal.

voyage.name: McGill University Campus
voyage.address: 805 rue Sherbrooke ouest at ave McGill College
voyage.content: The lower section of McGill's campus is composed mainly of 19th-century neoclassical buildings and is definitely worth a ten-minute stroll.

voyage.name: The Underground City
voyage.content: Throughout the downtown area. This network of underground malls and passageways is a very convenient way to walk around during the winter months. It encompasses six metro stations on the green and orange lines and all of the major downtown shopping malls, including food courts, cinemas, innumerable boutiques, and services.

voyage.name: Christ Church Cathedral
voyage.content: It is a small, but colourful church, the mother church of the region's Anglican (Episcopalian) denomination. Of special interest is the organ with additional remote-controlled organ pipes in the front of the church. If you have the opportunity to listen to an organ concert there, you should go. The concert will probably be by donation only.

voyage.name: Mary Queen of the World Cathedral
voyage.content: A 1/4 scale copy of St. Peter's in Rome. Impressive interior.

voyage.name: Canadian Centre for Architecture
voyage.price: $10 adults, $7 seniors, free for students and children
voyage.content: Architecture museum and research institute that incorporates the Shaughnessy House, an 1876 Second Empire-style manison. Across boulevard René-Lévesque from the CCA is a sculpture garden with works designed around the theme of architecture. Guided tours available.

voyage.name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.hours: Tue, Thu-Sun 10:00-17:00, Wed 10:00-21:00* (*only exhibits open from 17:00-21:00). Closed Mon
voyage.content: Many prominent travelling exhibits.

voyage.name: McCord Museum
voyage.content: Museum dedicated to Canadian history, next to McGill University.

voyage.name: Musée d'art contemporain de Montréal
voyage.price: $15 adult, $12 senior (60+), $10 students (18+ with ID), free for children (0-12), $5 youth (13-17), $30 family, children free
voyage.content: Contemporary art museum at the Place-des-Arts complex.

voyage.name: Redpath Museum
voyage.content: A museum of natural history on the McGill campus.

voyage.name: Windsor Station
voyage.content: This Romanesque Revival building served as one of the city's main railway stations until it was cut off from the rail network by the construction of the Bell Centre nearby.

voyage.name: Habitat 67
voyage.content: This visually striking residential building was created by architect Moshe Safdie for Expo 67. The result was an amazingly modern dwelling that challenged the way architects created urban homes. Compared alternately to a beehive, a Taos pueblo, and a crystalline growth, the complex's 154 units are composed of prefabricated concrete cubes assembled on site. The apartments here are highly prized and a number of promine

voyage.name: Place Sun-Yat-Sen
voyage.address: rue de la Gauchetière and rue Clark
voyage.content: A small public square in the middle of Chinatown. There are murals made of grey slate along the north and east side of the square; also at the square is a pavilion selling typical Chinatown tourist souvenirs.

voyage.name: Chalet du Mont-Royal
voyage.address: up the stairs from Redpath Crescent
voyage.content: Built as a make-work project in 1932 during the Great Depression. The interior features artwork depicting various scenes from Canadian history.

voyage.name: Kondiaronk Lookout
voyage.address: next to the Chalet du Mont-Royal
voyage.content: Offers panoramic views of the downtown Montreal skyline.

voyage.name: Croix du Mont-Royal
voyage.content: A white illuminated cross installed in 1924 at the site where Paul Chomedey de Maisonneuve planted a wooden cross in 1643. He allegedly planted it there after praying to the Virgin Mary to spare the city of Montreal from a flood.

voyage.name: Lac des Castors
voyage.content: Man-made lake in a former marsh. Paddleboats are rented out in summer; in winter the lake becomes an ice skating rink.

voyage.name: Monument à George-Étienne Cartier
voyage.address: along chemin Olmsted on the east side of Parc du Mont-Royal
voyage.content: A 1919 monument sculpted by George William Hill in honor of Georges-Étienne Cartier, one of the fathers of Confederation.

voyage.name: Belvédère Camillien-Houde
voyage.address: voie Camillien-Houde across from Cimetière Mont-Royal
voyage.content: Another lookout point.

voyage.name: Maison Smith
voyage.address: near Chemin Remembrance and voie Camillien-Houde

voyage.name: Bell Centre
voyage.content: Home of the Montreal Canadiens ice hockey team, commonly known as the Habs. Also hosts larger concerts.

voyage.name: Molson Stadium
voyage.content: An outdoor Canadian football stadium on the McGill campus. The McGill Redbirds (Quebec University Football League) and the Montreal Alouettes (Canadian Football League) play here.

voyage.name: Montreal Forum / Pepsi Forum
voyage.content: An entertainment complex at the site of the former home of the Canadiens from 1926-1996. It is home to an AMC Cinema (22 screens) and The Montreal Comedy Nest.

voyage.name: Boutique Eva B
voyage.content: Selections from local designers, vintage, and a bistro/bar thrown in for good measure. It's mostly just a thrift shop.

voyage.name: Café Presto
voyage.content: The best downtown deal for a very inexpensive and very satisfying casual/cozy Italian fare (main courses are all $5.95. Calculate approximately $20 if you add a glass of wine and an espresso). Very busy during lunchtime on weekdays. Arrive before noon or after 13:30 to avoid the longest lines. Cash only (no credit or debit cards, but there are a few ATMs on the same block).

voyage.name: Café Crystal
voyage.content: Light meals for breakfast and lunch. $5-7, close to the rue Sainte-Catherine shopping district.

voyage.name: Cafe Dizengoff
voyage.content: Kosher cafe on the ground floor of the Hillel House, on the McGill campus.

voyage.name: Dunn's Famous
voyage.content: Opened in 1927. It has smoked meat and poutine dishes.

voyage.name: Il Focolaio
voyage.content: Delicious pizza, wine and tiramisu.

voyage.name: SAT
voyage.content: This one-of-a-kind venue is supported by the province of Quebec and the federal government to display and promote digital art. With high ceilings and low couches, it has the feel of a funky, uber-hip techno club. In fact, there is quite a bit of great club music on weekend nights. But there's also fascinating computer art installations going on at all times, with some video and live performances. A great place to mee

voyage.name: Bar des Pins
voyage.hours: Daily 17:00-03:00, sometimes closes earlier on weekdays
voyage.content: Blue-collar bar invaded regularly by beer-pong-playing university students. Sells only cheap beer. Hottest night of the week is Tuesday.

voyage.name: Vinyl
voyage.content: Vinyl is a small, intimate club with frequent specials including $3 Rhum-n-Tings on Sunday nights and a diverse range of music from Reggae to Techno on different nights. Also, couches in the bathroom and an outdoor terrace around the back.

voyage.name: The Cock n' Bull
voyage.content: Inexpensive pub with a small kitchen, live bands, a single pool table and a couple of active dart boards. Known for their cheap 4 Liters beer pitchers (16 $). Friendly and sociable, for the most part English-speaking patrons, from age 18 to 60. Arts and crafts on Monday nights!

voyage.name: McKibbin's Irish Pub
voyage.content: Being next door to Concordia University may or may not be a point in its favor, but there's no denying that this friendly pub is a great place for a pint. The food is above-average for a pub, too. McKibbin's is known for their ladies night every Wednesday with its all night open bar ($10 cover for girls and $25 cover for guys).

voyage.name: Hurley's
voyage.content: Probably the best Irish pub in Montreal, with live traditional music every night and excellent food at fair prices. There's an upstairs for the busy nights, in addition to outdoor patios in the front and back. A part of the pub is non-smoking. Very cozy with a highly authentic feel and friendly professional staff.

voyage.name: Brutopia
voyage.content: Brewpub with their own beers on tap on the busy Crescent strip. English-speaking college crowd.

voyage.name: Peel Pub
voyage.content: Montreal legend. Sports bar. Dirt cheap specials. Good time, particularly on $1 shooter Thursdays.

voyage.name: Reggie's Bar
voyage.content: Concordia University's bar. Features special Hockey nights, and cheap Thursday beer and shots. Great part of student-life experience.

voyage.name: Le Vieux Dublin
voyage.content: Don't let the Vieux Dublin sign outside fool you — this pub is not one bit Irish. There's not a lot of Emerald Island schlock around, but the pints are good, and home-style meals for lunch and dinner really hit the spot. There's live music on weekends on the minuscule stage, but during the week it's quiet and comfy. Staff is polite and nice.

voyage.name: Time Supper Club
voyage.content: The first Supper Club in the city, Time Supper Club starts as a restaurant and slowly turns into a night club.

voyage.name: La Boom
voyage.content: One of the trendiest clubs in Montreal. Be well-dressed and have a well-dressed wallet.

voyage.name: Pang Pang Karaoke Bar
voyage.content: Very comfy rooms in a range of sizes can be hired by the hour, from $30.

voyage.name: K-Karaoke
voyage.content: Large rooms with clean decoration.

voyage.name: Abri du voyageur Hotel
voyage.content: Charming hotel for budget-conscious travellers. Renovated historical building recommended by many guides as an excellent value with a personal touch.

voyage.name: HI-Montréal
voyage.content: Friendly and helpful staff. Activities organized every day (pub crawls, bike tours, urban walks, etc.) Dormitories and private rooms.

voyage.name: University Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: Private rooms with shared bathroom and apartment suites with private bathroom, kitchenette and private entrance.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa
voyage.content: Continental breakfast.

voyage.name: Le Centre Sheraton Montreal Hotel
voyage.content: Offers 825 renovated rooms, free internet use in the Link@Sheraton lobby connectivity hub.

voyage.name: Marriott Residence Inn Montreal Downtown
voyage.content: With fully equipped kitchens and complimentary daily hot and cold buffet breakfast, Free WiFi access, rooftop terrace, laundry facility, friendly multi-lingual staff,

voyage.name: Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth
voyage.content: Offering 1,037 rooms, of which 100 are suites. Offers a health club, an indoor pool, and three restaurants: Les Voyageurs lounge, Le Montréalais bistro-restaurant and Beaver Club.

voyage.name: Hotel Le Dauphin Montréal Centre-Ville
voyage.content: Modern hotel with spacious rooms and a high level of service, within walking distance of the Old Town and modern city centre. Rooms are equipped with tea/coffee service, an Apple TV unit, and a computer. Rates include breakfast, newspapers, and wireless Internet access. Substantial discounts available for booking through the hotel’s web site.

voyage.name: Hotel (10)
voyage.content: A modern hotel with great design near boulevard Saint-Laurent.

voyage.name: Hotel Le Germain Montreal
voyage.content: A chic and intimate boutique-hotel designed for a hip clientele of leisure and business travelers.

voyage.name: Loews Hotel Vogue
voyage.content: Close to the corner of rue Sainte-Catherine.

voyage.name: Le Meridien Versailles-Montreal
voyage.content: This boutique hotel is in the chic Golden Square Mile neighborhood. This hotel features 108 rooms.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Montreal
voyage.content: Attached to the Complexe Desjardins.

voyage.name: Hotel Omni Mont-Royal
voyage.content: This five-star, four-diamond luxury hotel is centered amongst fashionable boutiques, museums, fine dining, and the exciting nightlife of Montreal's chic rue Crescent.

voyage.name: Ritz-Carlton Montreal
voyage.content: A historic luxury hotel, opened in 1912, that has played host to many famous figures such as Elizabeth Taylor, Winston Churchill and Queen Elizabeth II.

voyage.name: Grande Bibliothèque du Québec
voyage.content: The inviting, super-modern home to the Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec, a massive library housing four million works. The building itself is a contemporary style building integrating art and architecture including a glass mural, a kinetic luminous mural, a sculpture garden, and varying museum-style displays in the lower-level gallery. The tiles that cover the outside of the building are made to resemble

voyage.name: Galerie de l'UQAM
voyage.content: Contemporary art exhibits, workshops, lectures, and tours.

voyage.name: Écomusée du fier monde
voyage.content: A museum focused on the industrial and working-class history of Montreal (the name literally translates to Ecomuseum of the Proud People), particularly of the surrounding Centre-Sud district (basically the modern-day Le Village and Sainte-Marie neighborhoods). The museum is housed in the Bain Genereux, a 1920s art deco former indoor public pool. Note that unlike most Montreal museums, the exhibits here are only descr

voyage.name: Cinémathèque québecoise
voyage.price: Exhibitions free; film screenings $8 adults, $7 seniors (65+)/students, $5 children (6-15), free for children 5 and under
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun regular showing 17:00, exhibition hall Tue-Fri 11:00-20:00 and Sat Sun 16:00-20:00
voyage.content: Modern theater complex with 17-screens (most shows in French only), cafe, restaurant and bar.

voyage.name: Cinéma Cineplex Odeon Quartier Latin
voyage.content: Showcases mostly mainstream Hollywood films, all dubbed in French.

voyage.name: Théâtre Saint-Denis
voyage.content: Performing arts centre with two halls.

voyage.name: Maison de la culture Frontenac
voyage.content: Cultural centre in Sainte-Marie. Many free shows. Music, dance, cinema, theatre, etc.

voyage.name: Chlorophylle Montréal
voyage.content: One of two flagship 'concept stores' for Quebec-based outdoor clothing company with shirts, coats, and pants for men, women and children. Their environmentalism even extends to their dressing room-- made out of recycled barn sheds from Northern Quebec.

voyage.name: Boutique Woodstock
voyage.content: One of the many head-shops along Saint-Denis with all your 'smoking accessories' as well as hemp products including shirts, jeans, bags, and cosmetics.

voyage.name: Chez Gatsé
voyage.content: Set just below eye level, one of Montreal's only Tibetan restaurants offers momos (Tibetan dumplings), butter-tea, as well as exotic vegetarian and meat dishes spiced with ginger, garlic, and peppers. In the summer there's a shady terrace in the back.

voyage.name: Comptoir 21
voyage.content: The fish and chips restaurant offers delicious fresh fishes. One can sit outisde on the street in the middle of the Gay Village.

voyage.name: Villa Frontenac
voyage.content: Sainte-Marie diner with a large variety of plates (local, Italian, Greek, American, fast food, etc.).

voyage.name: Restaurant Bercy
voyage.content: Cheap diner food in a strip mall in Sainte-Marie.

voyage.name: Au Petit Extra
voyage.content: Exquisite French bistro cuisine at reasonable price, relaxed and friendly atmosphere that is very popular with locals. Excellent selection of wines.

voyage.name: Brioche Lyonnaise
voyage.content: A popular, reasonably-priced eatery, it can get crowded at times. Sandwiches, crepes.

voyage.name: Les 3 Brasseurs
voyage.content: Two terraces and four beers micro-brewed on site have made this upscale pub a popular place for dinner and lunch. Usual pub-fare with a European angle.

voyage.name: Mikado
voyage.content: Sushi, tempura, and other Japanese favorites.

voyage.name: Pub Sainte-Élisabeth
voyage.content: Best terrasse for a drink. Feels like a greenhouse. Great prices despite being in a busy area.

voyage.name: Foufounes Électriques
voyage.content: The name is a never-ending source of comedy for Montrealers and visitors alike, chiefly because of the stark difference in meaning between the French and French-Canadian interpretations of the term "foufounes." To locals, i.e. French-Canadians, the term is simply an endearing reference to one's posterior. However, to the French, the term is a rather explicit reference to female genitalia, which is always worth a few

voyage.name: L'Amère à Boire
voyage.content: Fine brew pub in the Quartier Latin, the beer is consistently good. On the menu: lagers and ales inspired from Czech, German, and English styles. Nice decor with wooden tables.

voyage.name: Le Cheval Blanc
voyage.content: Good brewpub located a few blocks east of busy rue Saint-Denis. Has been open for over 30 years.

voyage.name: Cafe Hookah
voyage.hours: Summer: 13:00-03:00 daily; rest of year: Sun-Tue 13:00-01:00, Wed 13:00-02:00, Thu-Sat 13:00-03:00
voyage.content: Smoking fruit-flavoured tobacco in an Arabic water pipe, while sipping a Grand Marnier is a fine way to spend the evening. A pipe is $6.50, you can smoke it alone or share it with a few people. They won't replace the coal though, so a pipe doesn't last very long, but they justify this by saying it makes it (comparatively) cheap to sample lots of flavours from their extensive menu.

voyage.name: Le Saint Bock
voyage.content: A brewpub having 20 beers on tap at all times: the pub's beers (usually 7 of them), plus beers from all around Quebec (usually 13 of them). Nice selection of privatelly imported beers from all around the world. Food is good with some nice touches of originality (have "the Graal") for reasonable prices. It may get loud during the night, and it is fully crowded on game nights — don't even think about watching a play-of

voyage.name: Cafe Campus
voyage.content: Best known for its Tuesday night discount pitchers, retro music, and lack of memories.

voyage.name: Stereo
voyage.content: Mainly plays house music and occasionally trance/techno. Stereo was once voted #5 of the top 10 clubs in the world by Muzik magazine, as it has welcomed several of the top DJs from around the world. The venue is known to have one of the best sound systems in North America. The crowd is mostly gay/lesbian depending on the night, the age ranges between 20-35, and is often at full capacity. A great place to end the nigh

voyage.name: Circus
voyage.content: Electronica and hip-hop. A luxuriously decorated after-hour in Montreal. Lots of space and hidden corners. The crowd is a bit younger (18-25), and doesn't always pack to full capacity. The venue has welcomed a number of big DJs.

voyage.name: Unity
voyage.price: Free admission on F before 22:30 and Sa before 23:00
voyage.content: The dance club in the village with a male erotic dancers downstairs.

voyage.name: Sky
voyage.content: Great roof bar with several floors to enjoy.

voyage.name: Le Stud Bar
voyage.content: Caters to leather and manly bear clientèle, though not exclusively leather.

voyage.name: Aigle Noir
voyage.content: Caters mostly to a male leather clientèle.

voyage.name: Cabaret Mado
voyage.content: A drag show with outrageous spectacles every night, run by the city's chief drag queen, Mado Lamotte.

voyage.name: Auberge de Paris Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Mixed, male, and female dorms available. Private rooms also available. Female dorm rooms have private bathrooms for exclusive use. Note that the reception desk is at 901 rue Sherbrooke est, inside the Hotel de Paris (see below).

voyage.name: Auberge Montréal Espace Confort
voyage.content: Private room with bathroom and small kitchen.

voyage.name: Hotel du Manoir St-Denis
voyage.content: A clean, modern, comfortable room with color cable TV, telephone, air conditioning, hair dryer, fridge, private bathroom, continental breakfast, and high speed wireless internet.

voyage.name: Hotel Viger Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: A clean modern, comfortable room with color cable-TV, telephone, air conditioning, hair dryer, fridge, private bathroom, continental breakfast and high speed wireless internet.

voyage.name: Le Jazz St Denis Hotel
voyage.content: Backpackers hostel in Montreal's Latin Quarter. Free wifi, free bagels, and free coffee all day. Has budget and deluxe private rooms as well as standard dormitories.

voyage.name: Le Simone
voyage.content: Friendly Bed and Breakfast with great breakfast, especially on weekends.

voyage.name: Atmosphère
voyage.content: Bed and breakfast offers private rooms with shared bathroom. Gourmet three-course breakfast included.

voyage.name: Hotel de Paris
voyage.content: Private bathrooms, cable TV, telephone, air-conditioning.

voyage.name: Hotel Lord Berri
voyage.content: All rooms come with air conditioning, cable TV, and free wireless internet. Choice of rooms with shared bath in the hall or suites with private path.

voyage.name: Montreal Biosphère
voyage.content: The former United States pavilion from Expo 67, a geodesic dome designed by R. Buckminster Fuller. It now houses an Environment Canada museum dedicated to water and the environment.

voyage.name: Habitat 67
voyage.content: This visually striking residential building was created by architect Moshe Safdie for Expo 67. The result was an amazingly modern dwelling that challenged the way architects created urban homes. Compared alternately to a beehive, a Taos pueblo, and a crystalline growth, the complex's 154 units are composed of prefabricated concrete cubes assembled on site. The apartments here are highly prized and a number of promine

voyage.name: Formula 1 Grand Prix
voyage.content: The Canadian Grand Prix or Formula One is a must-see for any petrolhead or sports fan. It attracts up to 100,000 people and spans a weekend, with practice and qualifying on Friday and Saturday and the race on Sunday. Wheelchair-accessible seats are available. The next most recent F1 is 21-23 May 2027.

voyage.name: Montreal Casino
voyage.content: Opened in 1993, this is the largest casino in Canada. Open to visitors aged 18 or older.

voyage.name: Osheaga Music and Arts Festival
voyage.content: A three-day indie & alternative rock festival held annually in Parc Jean-Drapeau on Île Sainte-Hélène at the end of July/beginning of August.

voyage.name: Public pool
voyage.hours: 16 Jun-24 Aug: daily 11:00-16:00, 25 Aug-14 Sep: Sat Sun 11:00-16:0

voyage.name: Beach park
voyage.price: Ages 14 and up $8, 6-13 $4, 65+ $7, family $20. Season passes available
voyage.content: Clean water and sand attracts families to this small, man-made beach at the south tip of Ile Notre Dame. Activities include a playground, volleyball, and watercraft rentals. There are bathrooms, changing rooms, and a snack bar.

voyage.name: Île Notre-Dame lake and at the Olympic Basin.
La Ronde
voyage.price: Discounts are readily available: a Coca-Cola tin is worth an $8 discount on any rides ticket
voyage.content: An amusement park that is a member of the Six Flags chain.

voyage.name: Snack Bar Espace-Bouffe
voyage.content: Basic chips-and-hot-dog snack bar.

voyage.name: La Bonne Carte
voyage.hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:00-14:30, dinner Sun-Thu 16:30-closing, brunch Sat 11:00-14:30, Sun 11:00-15:30
voyage.content: Lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch are offered at the Casino buffet.

voyage.name: Nuances
voyage.content: French haute cuisine with a Quebec edge served far removed from the noise of the casino. Choose between lobster, Quebec lamb, loin of deer, and other season specialties or try the chefs "discovery menu". Note, no exceptions are made to the Casinos: strict 18 & up policy.

voyage.name: Festin du Gouverneur
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: daily 18:00 and 20:30; Nov-Mar: daily 18:00; Dec: Sun-Thu 19:00, Fri Sat 18:30 and 20:30
voyage.content: Set menu (meat, fish, and veggie options) with historical reenactment show.

voyage.name: Parc Jeanne-Mance
voyage.address: between ave du Parc, ave du Mont-Royal, ave de l'Esplanade, and ave des Pins
voyage.content: Located in the western part of the Plateau, adjacent to Parc du Mont-Royal. At the corner of Mont-Royal and Parc is an art deco fountain dedicated in honour of Louis Rubenstein, the father of Canadian figure skating.

voyage.name: Parc Lafontaine
voyage.address: between ave du Parc Lafontaine, rue Rachel, ave Papineau, and rue Sherbrooke
voyage.content: Located in the eastern part of the Plateau, the park is well-manicured and includes an artificial lake, bike paths, sporting facilities, and an outdoor amphitheater. Very popular during summer.

voyage.name: Carré Saint-Louis
voyage.address: between ave Laval, rue Saint-Denis, and the two sides of rue du Square Saint-Louis
voyage.content: A smaller park, Carré Saint-Louis is at the east end of the Prince Arthur pedestrian mall, next to rue Saint-Denis. Though a fraction of the size of either Parc LaFontaine or Parc du Mont-Royal, it is a popular and scenic local destination. Two fountains, bike paths, and easy access to a number of restaurants and shops provide a comforting background and a relaxing setting. On a side note, many of the gags on the tel

voyage.name: Mount Royal Park
voyage.content: Has an artificial lake, many paths through the wood, and the best view on the city of Montreal.

voyage.name: Place Roy
voyage.address: rue Roy est and rue Saint-André
voyage.content: Public art piece in a small square featuring a stone map of the world and several scattered bronze chairs.

voyage.name: Maison de la culture du Plateau-Mont-Royal
voyage.content: Exhibits local artists.

voyage.name: Théâtre de Verdure
voyage.address: in Parc Lafontaine near rue Duluth and ave du Parc-Lafontaine
voyage.content: 3000-seat outdoor theater open for a summer program of dance, music, movies, and theater. Plan to line up early for the popular symphonies in the park series or just join the crowd of picnickers on the grass around the lake.

voyage.name: Main Madness
voyage.hours: One weekend in June and August
voyage.content: Two weekends each summer St-Laurent boulevard is closed to cars for the Main Madness street fair. More an overgrown sidewalk sale than fair, restaurants, and shops set up in the middle of the street.

voyage.name: L'Original
voyage.content: Non-profit gallery of works by living artists, with a strong focus on Montreal street art. Sister location to the gallery on rue Saint-Paul in Old Montreal.

voyage.name: Quartier Mode
voyage.price: Locally made accessories $18-60, locally made quality, well made dresses $80-189, mostly under $200. Except for more detailed, fully lined winter coats $168-289
voyage.content: Here you can find over 32 locally made independent Montreal designers; clothing for women, well made dresses, pretty accessories and a view into Montreal's fashion community. The owner is a passionate local designer who loves making people happy and finding the right piece for her customers.

voyage.name: Lustre
voyage.content: A local designer boutique

voyage.name: Friperie
voyage.content: Vintage.

voyage.name: Beatnick
voyage.content: Used records and CDs.

voyage.name: Paul's Boutique
voyage.content: Used CDs, records, and vintage T-shirts.

voyage.name: Mycoboutique
voyage.content: Describing themselves as the "General Store of the Mushroom," they feature all things fungal. In addition to the mushroom and truffle products you might find in more general gourmet food stores, there is an entire shelf of dried wild Canadian mushrooms, including several types from Quebec. Moreover, they promote the use and foraging of mushrooms and have books and other information on offer. The staff are very knowle

voyage.name: Vélo Québec
voyage.content: Good coffee and espresso, plus maps, bicycle kit and free air. Outside seating and plenty of free bicycle parking.

voyage.name: Cremerie Meu Meu
voyage.content: Ice cream and gelato is sold in this little shop.

voyage.name: Les Givres
voyage.content: This artisanal ice cream shop sells gourmet organic products including tasty cakes. The sorbets like the handpicked rhubarb or the "bleuets" are as good as the café or the chocolate choices.

voyage.name: Ripples
voyage.content: The little shop serves homemade ice cream.

voyage.name: Aux Vivres
voyage.content: The restaurant serves fresh vegan cuisine. There are many sandwich choices including the classic coconut grilled BLT or salads. Many things can be taken for the go. In the backyard there is a small outside terrasse.

voyage.name: La Banquise
voyage.content: La Banquise consistently tops locals' lists for best poutine in town (and not just because it's open for post-bar-hopping munch fests when judgment is slightly impaired). Maybe it's because they've been at it since 1968. The clientele is hip and clubworn, the walls and tables are brightly coloured, and the staff is friendly. 25 varieties of poutine make up most of the menu, but if you insist there are hamburgers and

voyage.name: La Binerie
voyage.content: A small unpretentious eatery that became a legend. It features traditional meals for under $10, especially fèves aux lard (beans cooked overnight with bacon).

voyage.name: Frite Alors!
voyage.content: Pommes frites with a choice of a half-dozen toppings. Poutine. Burgers. Salads. Part of a small local chain.

voyage.name: Maam Bolduc
voyage.content: Quebecois food include what just may be the best poutine in town, served in a dozen different varieties ranging from traditional to bourguignonne (with mince, mushrooms, and red wine sauce). The portions are huge and the $10.99 régulière is plenty for most ordinary people.

voyage.name: Santropol
voyage.content: This favorite Montreal spot serves a great selection of creative, gigantic sandwiches, soups, coffees, teas, and breads to appeal to any veggie palate. With a funky decor, a great outdoor garden in the back in the summer, bookshelves stocked with used books, and a food service for the needy, this casual restaurant is a veritable Montreal institution. Casual. Popular among students.

voyage.name: Schwartz's
voyage.content: Famous delicatessen for smoked meat, served up in huge, juicy, peppery slabs. No reservations. Expect to wait for a table at most times, but the queue moves fast. Smoked meat sandwich 16$. A good tip: locals get their sandwiches or smoked meat at the take-away counter to the left of the restaurant entrance. It moves a lot faster, it's a bit cheaper - and you get the exact same sandwich!

voyage.name: Soupesoup
voyage.content: Best soup and sandwich in town. Not cheap, but great quality and definitely original.

voyage.name: Chez Claudette
voyage.content: Delicious poutine and burgers, reasonable prices, and a shorter line than La Banquise. Friendly servers who also happen to be great at crowd control once the bars close.

voyage.name: Au Pied de Cochon
voyage.content: Modern restaurant with casual ambiance. Huge meals. The place to go for lamb and original Quebec cuisine for a reasonable price; the poutine with foie gras is particularly (in)famous. Advance reservations strongly recommended.

voyage.name: Beautys Luncheonette
voyage.content: A classic American brunch restaurant open since 1942, features a huge line-up. Regular people use to eat salmon bagels. The owner Hymne will seat you. While waiting you'll find postcards and reviews from all over the world including from Albert Prince of Monaco.

voyage.name: Byblos
voyage.content: One of the best unknown restaurants in Montreal. Prices are amazingly reasonable for the food quality. Iranian food.

voyage.name: Chez Doval
voyage.content: Portuguese grill.

voyage.name: Chu Chai
voyage.content: A treat for vegetarians, vegans, and those who love them. Chu Chai specializes in Thai cuisine made with soy or vegetable protein to simulate meat. The roast "duck" is delicious, and the tom yum gai (lemongrass soup with "chicken") warms the heart. A bistro and takeout counter next door called "Chuch" has the same dishes in a more casual setting and is "bring your own wine".

voyage.name: Eduardos
voyage.content: Good Italian restaurant, bring your wine!

voyage.name: Khyber Pass
voyage.content: Afghan. Bring your own wine.

voyage.name: L'Avenue
voyage.content: Famous for their eggs Benedict.

voyage.name: Le Poisson Rouge
voyage.content: A seafood BYOB with a wonderful prix fixe. The maitre d' is friendly and knows everything about each fish and its preparation.

voyage.name: Le Majestique
voyage.content: Highly rated kitsch-nautical-themed retro diner serving oysters and other tapas-style eats and offerings from a full bar, open late.

voyage.name: La Chronique
voyage.content: Has a casual feel until you see the astonishing creations of master chef Marc de Canck of Belgium. The table d'hôte with wines is perfect in just about every way, but don't get it if you have to ask what it costs.

voyage.name: L'Express
voyage.content: A real French bistro with a zinc bar. Tartare, moules, quiche, rilettes. A splurge, but worth it.

voyage.name: Bily Kun
voyage.content: Bily Kun — the name is Czech, meaning "White Horse" — is an institution in Montreal's Plateau district. Dim lighting, candles, and a huge bar give an intimate atmosphere, but Bily Kun gets hopping after 22:00 with Montreal's hippest Francophones practically every night. Some of the area's top DJs spin experimental or loungey techno, but there's really no dance floor to speak of. Bar staff is kooky and nice, even if n

voyage.name: Quai des Brumes
voyage.content: Very small and comfy watering hole in the heart of St. Denis near Parc du Mont-Royal. Velvet drapes, wood finish, and a chrome bar. Sometimes has live entertainment, which becomes a very intimate experience due to the small size.

voyage.name: Casa Del Popolo/La Sala Rossa
voyage.content: Established in September 2000, Casa Del Popolo is Montréal's only family-run neighborhood vegetarian hot-spot! Part fair-trade café, part music venue, part bar, part foosball hall. The Casa and its sister venue, La Sala Rossa, frequently host touring indie artists. Shows are cheap (sometimes free!). Try the goat cheese sandwich!

voyage.name: Le Réservoir
voyage.content: Brewpub. Very good snacks and tapas in a beautiful decor, there's a second floor upstairs.

voyage.name: Bifteck
voyage.content: Some of the cheapest beer in town, served with some of the saltiest popcorn in all of Creation, consumed by bohemians and students from near and far (and the occasional honest-to-God rock star). Great place to start or end a St-Laurent pub crawl: to the south, you'll find trendy, relatively expensive places; to the north, some of the best dive bars anywhere. Or you can just stay and get tanked.

voyage.name: Go Go Lounge
voyage.content: It's on the trendier part of St-Laurent, it looks trendy outwardly, the martini menu is certainly hip and happenin', but there's something missing: attitude. Anyone is made to feel welcome here and if there's a velvet rope and a doorman, it's only because the place really is full.

voyage.name: Else's
voyage.content: Small, cozy space with a great selection of draft beers and fine whiskeys. It's a restaurant, but you're better off eating elsewhere and just picking at the mandatory nosh (bowl of olives, etc.)

voyage.name: Dieu du Ciel
voyage.content: One of the best brew pubs in Montreal, it has a nice atmosphere for discussions between friends.

voyage.name: Le Salon Daomé
voyage.content: A little hard to find, small door leads to the nightclub upstairs. Tip: find the door man!

voyage.name: Muzique
voyage.content: A high-end destination, with 2 dance floors with eclectic DJ–spun beats, and a rooftop terrace overlooking Mount Royal

voyage.name: La Tulipe
voyage.content: Concert hall & club in a 1913 theatre, with themed dance nights, plus rock & jazz shows.

voyage.name: Auberge Chez Jean
voyage.content: Backpackers hotel with free breakfast and free wifi.

voyage.name: Le Bleu Balcon
voyage.content: Small, three-room, bed and breakfast in a typical Plateau apartment building. Shared bathrooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Stay Mont-Royal
voyage.content: European-style with shared bathrooms, free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Anne ma soeur Anne
voyage.content: Boutique studio-hotel.

voyage.name: A la Bonne Heure
voyage.content: Charming new bed and breakfast just above Parc Lafontaine, two blocks from Mont-Royal shopping, restaurants, nightlife. Only four rooms, so book ahead.

voyage.name: Chez Francois Bed and Breakfast
voyage.content: Located in the lower Plateau area, close to Duluth restaurants, Saint-Laurent nightlife and more. Five rooms in a typical Montreal walk up, lovingly maintained by Francois, an accommodating host who has excellent suggestions for tourists, as well as preparing wonderful complimentary breakfasts. Free parking available.

voyage.name: The Hôtel de l'Institut
voyage.content: Located between the Latin Quarter and Plateau Mont-Royal, facing one of Montréal’s most charming green spaces, Square Saint-Louis. Free breakfast.

voyage.name: Auberge de la Fontaine
voyage.content: Fun bed and breakfast with 25 rooms across the street from Parc Lafontaine.

voyage.name: Dante Park
voyage.content: Small park popular for its bocce court.

voyage.name: Church of the Madonna della Difesa
voyage.content: 1900s neo-Romanesque church built to commemorate the apparition of the Madonna in La Difesa, in Campobasso, Molise. Frescos by Guido Nincheri.

voyage.name: Marché Jean-Talon
voyage.content: The largest open-air market in North America, it is surrounded by other food businesses: meat, fish and cheese stores, bulk food emporia, dealers in spices and imported goods, bakeries, and restaurants. From May to October, its open-air arcades are occupied by about 300 vendors, mostly farmers from the countryside around Montreal.

voyage.name: Plaza St. Hubert
voyage.address: rue Saint-Hubert between rue Beaubien est and rue Jean-Talon est
voyage.content: Several blocks of discount clothing and household items with a scattering of fast food restaurants and cafes. A good place to find bargains, the specialty is bridal gowns and formal wear.

voyage.name: Pasticceria Alati-Caserta
voyage.content: Italian desserts and pastries, almond cake, Sicilian cannoli, Sfoglitella Napolitana, and biscotti. Since 1968.

voyage.name: Havre aux Glaces
voyage.content: Gelato

voyage.name: Whisky Cafe
voyage.content: Featuring not just whiskeys but also an extensive wine and port list. Whiskey Cafe is adjacent to one of the few cigar lounges in Montreal.

voyage.name: Vices & Versa Bistro Du Terroir Inc
voyage.content: Bistro on the edge of Little Italy featuring Quebec cuisine and home-made beer from small microbreweries.

voyage.name: À la Carte B&B
voyage.content: Stylish Bed and Breakfast in residential neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Concordia University - Loyola Campus
voyage.content: Concordia's western campus dating from 1916, which started out as Loyola College before merging with Sir George Williams University in 1974 to form Concordia University.

voyage.name: Westmount Square
voyage.address: rue Sainte-Catherine ouest at ave Wood
voyage.content: A four-building complex composed of black metal and glass, built in 1967 and designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

voyage.name: Westmount City Hall
voyage.content: It was designed by architects Francis R. Findlay and Robert Findlay in the Neo-Tudor style. Its style is reminiscent of Scottish castles, with its central tower and crenelations and turrets. It was completed in 1922.

voyage.name: Encore Books and Records
voyage.content: Used bookstore and record store. They carry books in English and French, although the English selection is a bit larger.

voyage.name: Chez Nick
voyage.content: A Montreal institution since 1920. Stop by for a hamburger, chili, or tuna melt.

voyage.name: La Louisiane
voyage.content: Cajun and creole cuisine.

voyage.name: Ristorante Maestro
voyage.content: Kosher.

voyage.name: Yakimono Sushi Bar
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 12:00-15:00 and 17:00-23:00, Sat 1 hr after Shabbat-01:30
voyage.content: Kosher sushi restaurant. Takeout and delivery available.
